Let \(w=d_9d_8\cdots d_0\) be the 10-digit representation of \(n\), allowing leading zeros.  
For each \(k\), writing \(n=10^k a + (d_{k-1}\cdots d_0)\), the condition becomes
\[
(d_{k-1}\cdots d_0)10^{10-k} > n.
\]
This says exactly that \(w\) is lexicographically smaller than its suffix of length \(k\). Thus \(w\) must be lexicographically smaller than all of its proper suffixes, i.e. \(w\) is a Lyndon word of length \(10\) over an alphabet of \(10\) digits.

The number of Lyndon words of length \(m\) over \(q\) symbols is
\[
\frac1m \sum_{d\mid m} \mu(d) q^{m/d}.
\]
So with \(m=10,\ q=10\),
\[
\frac1{10}\left(10^{10}-10^5-10^2+10\right)
= \frac{9,999,899,910}{10}
= 999,989,991.
\]

\[
\boxed{999989991}
\]
